user: And what are the typical timelines?
answer:
For your dispute on TX-0401 (dispute ID 1, duplicate_charge, EUR 240.00):

- **Review target:** 10 business days, because duplicate_charge is a card reason code.
- **Complex cases:** If the transaction involves a foreign acquirer, review can take up to 45 calendar days. You would be notified if that happens.
- **Provisional credit:** Provisional credits are applied only to fraud-code disputes over EUR 50. This does not apply to a duplicate_charge dispute.

The case moves through these stages: open, under review, provisional credit, then resolved (upheld or declined). Only open or under-review cases can be withdrawn, and a withdrawal is final.

I can't give you an exact resolution date for this case. If you want a status update on dispute 1, I can escalate it to a human agent.

Dispute handling process
## Review timelines
The review target is 10 business days for card reason codes and 20 business
days for transfer reason codes. Complex cases involving a foreign acquirer may
run to 45 calendar days; the customer is notified when that happens.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each dispute reason code has its own window, counted in days from the
transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Complaints
## Acknowledgement and resolution
A complaint is acknowledged within one business day and resolved within 15
business days. Complex complaints may take up to 35 business days, with the
customer informed of the delay.

Dispute handling process
## Provisional credit
Where the disputed amount exceeds EUR 50 and the reason code is a fraud code, a
provisional credit is applied within two business days. Provisional credit is
reversed if the dispute is later declined.
